id: The Lily Shaw Quartet-Bedlam And Squalor, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: The Lily Shaw Quartet
long_description:
Fresh from three years of touring worldwide with Grammy-nominated band The Teskey Brothers, saxophonist and vocalist Lily Rose Shaw will be presenting a programme of original vocal jazz compositions, joined on stage by Hector McLachlan on keys, Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa on drums and Seth Boy on bass.

Lily's music has a strong foundation in jazz, and takes inspiration from a lifetime of eclectic musical interests, from classical to soul. Lily will be debuting new music for this special one-off, Jazz Festival performance in her hometown.

$15 online, $20 on the door


Part of the Wellington Jazz Festival 2026

id: Oscar Lavën: The Music Of Django Reinhardt-Saint Michael's Anglican Church, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Oscar Lavën: The Music Of Django Reinhardt
long_description:
Oscar Lavën and Les Tripes (French for 'The Guts') Present:

The Music of Django Reinhardt
Dynamic woodwind virtuoso Oscar Lavën joins forces with swing guitarist specialists Adrian Jensen & James Quick, and double bass raconteur Robert Henderson to present a homage to the unique music of guitarist Django Reinhardt and violinist Stephane Grapelli. Together they will create hard-working interpretations of the infectious, foot-stomping, film noir music known in 1940s Paris as Hot Club. This time, they're performing in the beautiful historic Saint Michael's Church.
6pm downbeat.

id: Li'l Chuck The One Man Skiffle Machine Wellington Capital Blues-Lynotts Irish Pub, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Li'l Chuck The One Man Skiffle Machine Wellington Capital Blues
long_description:
Official capital Blues info here
https://www.capitalblues.co.nz/.../lil-chuck-the-one-man.../
Official Jazz Festival info here https://www.jazzfestival.nz/.../lil-chuck-the-one-man.../
Li'l Chuck The One man Skiffle Machine is an authentic one man band performing “good time music with old time style”
Having spent a lifetime rummaging through the drawers of 1930's - 50's music, Chuck’s songs are inspired by the sounds of the era - Blues, Early Jazz, Western Swing, Ragtime etc. and are uniquely presented in the style of street performers from those glory days. Sticking to the traditional one man band format, Chuck plays all the instruments simultaneously.
Captivating storytelling intertwines effortlessly with heart stopping harmonica. Multiple guitar styles are underpinned by his left and right feet frantically pounding the kick and hi hat. The listener is left simply wondering, How the hell does he do that?
Originally hailing from the UK, Li’l Chuck has been stomping his music in NZ since 2003.
Stunning vocal stunning harmonica and acoustic guitar that needs no window dressing
Blues matters magazine (UK) May 2019
A true multi-instrumentalist & multi-tasker in addition to a talented artist.
No depression magazine USA. March 2017
Li'l Chuck combines almost every element of pure joy. 4 1/2 stars (out of 5)
NZlListener. March 2017.
Sublime harp and heartfelt vocals leave the listener wanting more
Blues matters magazine (UK) June 2017

id: [offsite] New Jazz For The New Era-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: [offsite] New Jazz For The New Era
long_description:
As part of the Wellington Jazz Festival, Pyramid Club presents three of Wellington's most creative and extraordinary contemporary jazz ensembles at Meow.

The Bridget Kelly Quintet features Bridget Kelly on reeds and harp, three double bassists (Tom Callwood, Isaac Smith and Patrick Bleakley) and drummer John Rae. Spirit Level is a new, interstellar duo of Daniel Beban (guitar) and Andy Wright (drums). And, led by free jazz luminary Anthony Donaldson, the Ghosts of Mount Kodak features Anton Wuts (saxophone), Kaito Walley (trombone), Dayle Jellyman (synths), Tom Callwood (bass) and Jonny Marks (voice and electronics).

Contemporary jazz at its best!

More info and tickets via the Jazz Festival Website.

id: Jazz Festival: April Phillips And Quintet-The Roxy Cinema, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Jazz Festival: April Phillips And Quintet
long_description:
I Can't Give You Anything But Love
Experience the epitome of NZ's capital jazz as this ensemble brings their sophisticated, sultry sound to the Wellington Jazz Festival stage in the gorgeous Art Deco ambience of The Roxy Cinema.

Fronted by the captivating April Phillips— with her rich & smooth tone, accompanied by a powerhouse five-piece band delivers an unforgettable evening of classic jazz, swing, and blues standards.

The band features award-winning pianist Anita Schwabe, Zak Dikvert on guitar, Russell Henderson on saxophone, Rory Macartney on bass, and Greg Crayford on drums, the band channels the cool, effortless vibe of a classic mid-century lounge, creating the ultimate, high-end festival experience.

And why not book a pre-dinner at The Roxy's fabulous COCO restaurant for an evening of the best jazz music.

id: Pōneke La Pompe-Superfina, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Pōneke La Pompe
long_description:
Pōneke La Pompe is Wellington’s answer to a smoky Parisian side street, 1930s edition, minus the smoke, plus a bit more Cuba Street chaos.

Named for Pōneke, one of the city’s Māori names, fused with “la pompe” (the relentless rhythm-guitar heartbeat of jazz manouche), the quartet steals shamelessly from Django Reinhardt and Stéphane Grappelli and gets away with it. Violinist Ana Henderson and clarinettist Josh Buckler duel it out on the melodies while guitarists Mike Kingston and David Harris hold the whole thing together with hands fast enough to set the strings on fire. Expect hot club standards, a few originals, and the kind of swing that makes sitting still very difficult.

Koha is welcomed :)

id: Jazz Festival: Song For Iqbal, Song For Pat - Miro Holland Group-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Jazz Festival: Song For Iqbal, Song For Pat - Miro Holland Group
long_description:
As part of Wellington Jazz Festival, The Undercurrent presents Song For Iqbal, Song For Pat - Miro Holland Group!

After a stellar year, an album release and Aus/Aotearoa tour, Miro Holland Group returns to the Festival with special guests. The band grew up learning to play together, and have continued. Miro's compositional theory is an attempt at highlighting that history. 

'Song For Iqbal, Song for Pat' is a dedication to both the philosopher Muhammad Iqbal -a major creative and moral influence for Miro- and to Miro's Great Aunt Pat, whose life was lived entirely in the service of others. Both figures are moral influences for Miro, though at different points in his development. 

Tonight, the group will feature two very special guests:

Lucas Kewell, an internationally acclaimed pianist fresh from completing studies at the renowned JAZZCAMPUS in Basel, Switzerland.
Patrick Bleakley, who has appeared on many internationally acclaimed albums, and had a legendary stint in the infamous Aotearoa group BLERTA.

Also featuring:
Ateo Buhne - Drums
Iggy Nama Ruci - Saxophone
Miro Holland - Trumpet & Composition
Theo Thompson - Guitar 

Come and hear the new music from Pōneke.

Friday Oct 16
Doors 4:30pm
Music 5pm
$15

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

id: Jazz Festival: Liam George Does Fred Wesley-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Jazz Festival: Liam George Does Fred Wesley
long_description:
As part of Wellington Jazz Festival, The Undercurrent presents Liam George Does Fred Wesley!

Get ready for an afternoon of high energy funk and jazz.

Liam George Does Fred Wesley is a powerhouse tribute to one of the greatest architects of funk. Backed by an all-star lineup of top local musicians, Liam George brings the unmistakable grooves, fiery horn lines, and deep soul of Fred Wesley to life.

From the legendary James Brown years to his adventures with Count Basie, this is music that demands to be felt as much as heard. Expect killer solos, unstoppable rhythms, and the kind of high-energy performance that keeps you moving from the first note to the last.

If you love funk, soul, jazz, or simply incredible live music, don't miss this celebration of one of the true masters.

Friday Oct 16
Doors 3pm
Music 3:30pm
$15

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆
